reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) comes from a single study on a bulk HfMoNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy, not on CrFeNiTi-based nanoparticles. It shows boron-induced intergranular borides improve grain boundary cohesion and ductility in that bulk system, but provides no direct support for the key premises regarding nanoscale synthesis, nanoparticle-specific grain boundary pinning, or stability under catalytic/thermoelectric cycling in the proposed composition.
premises: Boron segregates to grain boundaries in CrFeNiTi nanoparticles during synthesis
Boron forms stable intergranular boride precipitates at the nanoscale
These boride precipitates act as pinning centers that retard grain boundary motion
Pinning inhibits grain coarsening and atomic diffusion under high-temperature exposure
This mechanism preserves structural and chemical stability in the 773–1923 K range
